verdict:
SAFE TO START the full run with the command in RUN-FULL.md, after the fixes below. The partition, resume, admission and bounded handling hold. Three defects were fixed in run-resumable.mjs and RUN-FULL.md, and each fix was tested. One limit stays open: the memory reservation for an 8000 MB big part (8950 MB) is extrapolated from measurements at 400-2000 MB; check max_rss_mb in the first big parts' result files.

FIXED:
(a) Requirement 6. New flag --spawn-gap-ms (default 250). Before, up to --workers processes started at once and every part had its own process. Now the parts with estimate <= --batch-max-est (default 81; 3,750 of the 9,154 parts) run one after another in a host process, each in a fresh worker thread with the heap limit of --mem-mb. A host counts as one worker, and --batch-parts (default 100) replaces a host after that many parts. Also new: --plan-parts, which prints the part list as JSON. Building this, I hit a Node 24/Windows behaviour, verified with a probe: after an IPC disconnect a child emits 'exit' but never 'close'. My first version hung on it. The host is now ended by a message and handled on 'exit' or 'close', whichever comes first.
(b) Admission reserved S+150 MB per worker. Measured peak working sets were 550 MB at S=400, 1198 MB at S=1000 and 2254 MB at S=2000, because grown typed arrays are copied and the old copy is held until a collection. The reservation is now S + 150 + S/10.
(c) The memory-sampling timer was reset by every finished part, so working sets were never sampled while parts finished faster than every 5 s. The build's own r-full has max_rss_mb null in all 43 DF2-K2-R1 records. Sampling now runs every --poll-s regardless.

RUN-FULL.md was updated to match: command and flags, how it runs, admission, peak memory (about 7.2 GB normal, about 9 GB big), D2-K2-R1 marked new, and a test-evidence section for this check.

Convention: in mutations, a_test_failed is set as the brief defines it: true = the runner behaved correctly in that test. The return file is C:/Users/User/AppData/Local/Temp/claude/192654871f6b1294/e24f17dc-4aea-4914-a9d1-280a723d620e/scratchpad/tcb-build/done/runner-check.json.

findings.claim: The runner started up to --workers check.mjs processes in the same tick and one process per part. That is 9,154 process starts, about 4 a second through the 1,118 group-1 parts of about 1 s each. These are the short-lived process bursts that stalled the PC. There was no --spawn-gap-ms.
findings.evidence: The original schedule() started parts in a loop with no delay, and startPart spawned one process per part. After the fix: r-floor ran 43 parts in 2 host processes started 256 ms apart. r-full ran 86 parts with 16 process starts (4 hosts, 12 part processes), smallest gap 250 ms. r-proc (--batch-max-est 0) made 43 starts, smallest gap 251 ms. At most 2 parts ran at once (overlap.mjs).
findings.fix: FIXED. --spawn-gap-ms (default 250) allows at most one process start per gap. --batch-max-est (default 81) runs small parts one after another in a host process, each in a fresh worker thread with resourceLimits = --mem-mb and the same check.mjs --mem-mb. A host counts as one worker and is ended when idle or after --batch-parts (default 100) parts. Results are unchanged: A-ALARM via hosts and via 43 processes gave 0 per-part differences.

findings.lines: original 66-75, 292-297; now 84-95, 324-330; RUN-FULL.md Admission and Peak memory
findings.claim: Admission and RUN-FULL.md treated a worker of size S as S+150 MB, but its flags do not cap its memory: --max-old-space-size limits only the JS heap. check.mjs keeps its store in typed arrays, and grow() copies an array while the old copy stays until a collection. The real peak grows with S, so the documented peaks (6.6 GB normal, 8.2 GB big) were understated.
findings.evidence: Measured through the lane with process.resourceUsage().maxRSS: check.mjs A-FENCE-CE --bud k=1,cs=1 at --max-old-space-size=400 / --mem-mb 360 peaked at 550 MB while check.mjs counted 281 MB (tmp/model-check/mem400.err). The earlier, cut-off check measured 1198 MB at 1000 and 2254 MB at 2000 (mem1000.err, mem2000.err). That is S+150, S+198 and S+254.
findings.fix: FIXED. reserveOf(S) = S + 150 + ceil(S/10) is now used for admission, for the headroom of running workers, and in the start-up check: 590, 1250 and 2350 MB at the measured sizes, 1800 MB at 1500, 8950 MB at 8000. A big part now starts only with about 13 GB free. Not verified above 2000 MB: check max_rss_mb in the first big parts' result files.

findings.claim: Every schedule() call, one per finished part, cleared and re-armed the 5 s sampling timer. While parts finished faster than every 5 s, the working set was never sampled. Admission then counted full reservations, which is conservative, but the result files' max_rss_mb stayed null.
findings.evidence: In tmp/model-test/r-full/DF2-K2-R1/*.json, all 43 records have max_rss_mb null. After the fix, r-full and r-final have parts with rss figures.
findings.fix: FIXED. A separate poll timer is armed once and not reset by schedule(), and a separate gap timer handles --spawn-gap-ms.

mutations.what: (1) Partition: run-all.mjs with the fake-spawn preload (no real children) for A-ALARM, DF2-K3-R2 and D3-K4F-R2, against the runner's --plan-parts. 43/43, 140/140 and 343/343 parts: equal lists, none missing, none twice.
(1) Partition, all 77 configurations against the earlier full run-all spawn record: 9,154 = 9,154, 77 equal, 0 unequal.

(6) My first host version hung after 37 parts. Cause, confirmed by ipc-probe.mjs: after the parent disconnects the IPC channel, the child emits 'exit' but never 'close'. Fixed: the host is ended by a message and handled on exit or close.
(2) Uninterrupted reference r-full (A-ALARM + DF2-K2-R1, mixed hosts and processes): 86 parts complete, 4,073,127 states and 11,491,895 transitions, equal to run-all's figures. Exit 0.
(2) Killed by the lane's taskkill /T /F at 8 s after 65 parts. The restart reused those 65 and ran 21, with 0 per-part differences from r-full.
(2) Final code with --batch-parts 5: killed at 6 s after 53 parts, then restarted. 0 differences from r-full, at most 2 parts at once, and no node process of this check left afterwards.

(2) Damaged files: a torn file, a missing file with a complete tmp file beside it, a wrong fingerprint, another part's result, and a record marked bounded. Exactly the first four reran and the tmp file was removed. The bounded record was reported as BOUNDED with exit 1, never as complete. --rerun-bounded then gave exit 0 and 0 differences.
(3) --floor-mb 25000 with about 18.3 GB free: 0 process starts in 15 s and a 'waiting for memory' log. On the same folder, --floor-mb 12000 ran to completion.
(6) --batch-max-est 0: 43 part processes, smallest gap 251 ms, results equal to the 2-host run.

(4) --mem-mb 56 --big-mem-mb 58: all 43 parts were bounded, retried alone, and stayed BOUNDED with exit 1. A second start reran nothing. --big-mem-mb 400 reran them alone, one at a time, back to 413,666 states, exit 0.
(5) Memory: at size 400, a worker peaked at 550 MB of working set while check.mjs counted 281 MB. With 1198@1000 and 2254@2000, the original S+150 reservation is too small above 400 MB. Fixed (RC-2).
(5) Memory sampling never ran while parts finished quickly: max_rss_mb was null in the build's records. Fixed (RC-3).
(5) --plan gives 77 configurations and 9,154 parts in the documented order. D2-K2-R1 was wrongly marked as existing; fixed. At most --workers processes (hosts included), big parts alone.
